items.title: Peter Bocage Interview, 1962-02-06
items.q: Frankie took them over and called it the Eagle Band, see. He was a trombone player, see. Well instead of Bowling, he had a fella called Edward Clem, an old trumpet player. He was a figure too, you know, head man. Well then I played violin with them, with Eagle Band, see.

ctx.x: Do you remember who was in Buddy's band when you saw him?

I might remember a few of those fellas. I think he was Buddy, and the Runs of Stores, Bob Lyons, Cornish was playing trombone. I think Brock Mumford was playing, yes, Brock Mumford was playing guitar, and a fella called Frank Lewis was a clarinet player. And I think Jamesy Phillips up here played the drums. You see when Bowling went crazy, you know, he's the Hart and Jackson. Well Frankie Dewson took the band then. The same fellas that Bowling had, Frankie took them over and called it the Eagle Band, see. He was…
Was he a loud trumpet player? Yeah, oh yeah, he was loud.

items.title: Peter Bocage Interview, 1959-01-29
items.q: Well, a fella by the name of Edwild Clemmen, at that time.

ctx.x: Well, a fella by the name of Edwild Clemmen, at that time. And then, later on, Bunk went with the Eagle Band, too. Now, the funny thing about Bunk, when he was with us downtown, the Superior Band, he didn't drink, he didn't have no bad habits at all. And when he went uptown with the Eagle Band, they ruined him. He started drinking and he went all the pieces, you know? Just ruined himself. It showed you a different environment, you understand? Mm-hmm.
When he was with the Superior, was he a good reader?
